fileQuotes.text: Anchor one end of a barbell on the floor in a corner or landmine pivot so it cannot slide backward, load the other end with plates, and straddle the bar with the feet shoulder-width apart and the knees slightly bent.
Set a parallel-height box behind you inside a power rack and loop a band from each sleeve of a barbell down to the base of the rack or heavy dumbbells secured on the floor.

Place a dumbbell on the floor in front of a sturdy bar or upright, hold the support with both hands for balance, and stand with the ball of one foot on the dumbbell handle and the other foot lifted clear of the floor.

Because in an upright front squat to a bench the knees normally travel forward over the toes while tracking in the direction of the toes, that dated prohibition is deliberately left out of the draft instructions, and `"knees in line with the toes"` is kept as the direction the knees track.
Keeping your head up, your back straight, and your elbows high, bend the knees in line with the toes to lower slowly until your glutes touch the bench. Do not sit back and relax on the bench.
Immediately drive the hips and knees forward to stand tall, letting the kettlebell swing forward and up on a long, straight arm until it floats to chest or shoulder height with your shoulders square.
